notes.meaning: The prophet praises the Lord with all his heart for His wonderful deeds. Everything God has done was carefully planned long ago, and He has carried it out with absolute faithfulness. Believers can rest in the truth that God always keeps His promises.

God turns proud, heavily defended enemy cities into piles of broken stones. These strongholds of ruthless oppressors are laid waste and will never be rebuilt. Their ruin shows that no human power can stand against the Lord or permanently threaten His people.

When violent and powerful nations see how God judges the wicked, they are gripped with awe. Some former enemies are humbled and turn to worship the Lord, while others are forced to admit His supreme power. In the end, God's great deeds lead people everywhere to revere Him.

The Lord is a safe shelter for poor and helpless believers in their deepest distress. The attacks of cruel oppressors beat against them like a violent rainstorm hitting a strong wall, but God protects them from real harm. Even when trouble is fierce, God keeps His people safe and secure.

Just as a cloud brings welcome shade to cool scorched desert ground, God quickly quenches the raging fury of His enemies. He silences the loud shouting and proud victory songs of ruthless foes. His people can trust that no earthly oppressor will triumph over them for long.

On Mount Zion, which represents God's church and kingdom, the Lord prepares a rich banquet for people of all nations. He freely offers the best spiritual food and drink to nourish and delight every hungry soul. This celebration pictures the rich joy and fellowship God gives through the gospel.

differ.view: Reformed teachers see this feast as the spiritual blessings and comforts of the gospel enjoyed in the church.
Some evangelicals understand this banquet as a literal earthly feast celebrating Christ's final victory.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition connects this mountain feast with the celebration of the Eucharist in the Mass.

notes.meaning: The Lord promises to remove the thick sheet of spiritual darkness that hangs over all nations. For centuries, this covering kept people blinded by ignorance and false worship. Through the light of Christ, God opens people's eyes so they can see His truth clearly.

God will completely destroy death forever through the victory and resurrection of Christ. The Lord will gently wipe every tear from the eyes of His suffering people and remove their earthly disgrace. Because the Lord Himself has spoken, believers can be certain of eternal life and unending joy.

When this great salvation is revealed, God's people will shout aloud with joy and praise. They will rejoice because the God they patiently waited for has arrived to rescue them. Their patient trust will be richly rewarded with everlasting gladness in His presence.

God's protective hand will rest permanently on Mount Zion to bless and defend His people. At the same time, their proud enemies—represented by Moab—will be crushed down like straw trodden into a dung pit. The Lord will bring a shameful end to everyone who hates and persecutes His church.

The proud enemy is pictured as thrashing about helplessly, spreading out his arms like a swimmer trying not to sink in the filth. No matter how hard or skillfully he struggles, the Lord brings down all his pride. God proves that human cleverness cannot save anyone who sets himself against the Almighty.

The enemy's highest walls and strongest fortresses will be torn down and reduced to dust. No fortress made by human hands can withstand the mighty power of the Lord. God's people can take comfort knowing that every haughty power opposing them will eventually crumble.
